answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each agent gets a kernel of private state; on registration it must publish a commitment to that kernel. Challenges ask the agent to reveal a fresh, unpredictable function of kernel state. A clone sharing the kernel answers identically, so it cannot diverge, and colliding answers expose the shared origin. To survive, an attacker must give each identity its own kernel and answer every challenge independently, costing one full state initialization plus ongoing per-challenge computation per identity. A shared walnut of state cannot cover a lagoon of clones.
